lens: Typeform-style conversational wizard-first: one question per screen for setup and persona creation
name: Cadence Conversational Studio
one_liner: A one-question-at-a-time studio: personas are built by answering questions, then the live call runs in a calm dark cockpit with private coaching and visible scoring, built on shadcn/ui, Motion and Geist.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed: setup, onboarding and persona creation are Typeform-style, one question per screen, Enter to advance, with a permanent 'Skip all to form' escape. This follows Obvious' one-step-at-a-time creation flow (1/3 counter, Skip all) on Mobbin. Changed: the lens stops at the live call. A one-question rhythm fails mid-call, so the cockpit uses dense, scannable side-panel coaching like Fireflies' Sales Assist and Dialpad's transcript-plus-AI layout, with one primary action per state. Mobbin notice (show to user): 'Your Mobbin AI usage is high this month. Usage is unlimited during beta.'

design_language.typography: Geist Sans replaces Inter and Sora. Wizard questions 48/52 with -0.03em tracking on desktop and 30/36 on mobile; body 16/24; Geist Mono for timers, scores and timestamps. Only weights 400, 500 and 600.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 20px radius on cards and sheets, 12px on controls and chips, pill for status. Dark mode uses hairlines instead of shadows; light cards get one soft shadow at 6% opacity. Glow only on the active cue card.
design_language.motion: Wizard questions slide up 280ms ease-out and Enter advances. Cue cards enter from the right in 200ms and auto-dismiss after 8s unless pinned. Rubric bars spring on change. Reduced motion falls back to fades.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 20px with 1.75 stroke. One custom cue glyph, a speech bubble with a spark, reserved for coaching. No emoji in the app; illustration appears only on the landing page.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark by default on /call and debrief; light by default elsewhere. Tokens on :root with data-theme overrides, honoring prefers-color-scheme, with a header toggle.

navigation_and_ia: Top nav with four items: Practice, Library, Progress, Team (Team shown only when an org exists). Practice is a hub with 'Start a call' and a secondary 'Build a persona' action. Library lives at /library with filters synced to the URL (?job=sdr&industry=solar&difficulty=3&objection=price). The live call at /call/[id] is full-bleed with no nav, to protect focus. Debrief at /call/[id]/debrief. Cmd+K opens a palette across personas, calls and settings. Keys: Enter advances the wizard, Space is push-to-talk, Esc hides cues.

screens.layout: Paper-background hero, max 1200px. Left column: 56px Geist headline 'Say the hard sentence before it counts', one subhead, and a single input styled as a wizard question: 'What do you sell, and who do you call?' with an Enter hint. Right column: an animated call card with the caller orb, a cue card typing 'Ask about unit age first', and a live rubric bar at 72. Below the fold: a three-step strip (Pick a persona, Coach live, Debrief), a six-card library preview and an 'OpenAI in this app' model strip. Footer: contributor wall and 'Good first persona' issues.
screens.key_components: Hero question input, animated call-card demo, model strip, library preview, contributor wall, badges for MIT and OpenAI models.
screens.change_vs_today: Replaces the generic fake call card and four feature cards with a question that opens the wizard, and names the OpenAI models in the product.

screens.layout: Three zones. Left 240px filter rail with grouped facets: sales job (SDR cold call, AE discovery, CS renewal, collections, recruiting), industry (insurance, mortgage, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, retail), difficulty (1 to 5 dial), objection type (price, timing, competitor, authority, trust) and mode (voice or text). Top: command search and removable filter chips. Main: three-column card grid. Each card: monogram avatar tinted by industry, name and role, difficulty pips, two objection chips, expected length, Practice and Duplicate buttons. Last cell: 'Build one with AI'. Filters live in the URL.
screens.key_components: Command search, facet checkboxes, difficulty dial, removable filter chips, persona cards, URL-synced state, Build-with-AI card.
screens.change_vs_today: Replaces a three-item dropdown with a faceted library covering 15 sales jobs at launch, targeting 150+ personas.

screens.layout: Full screen with no nav. Top rail: thin progress bar, 'Step 3 of 7' and Save draft. Center: one 48px Geist question at a time, such as 'Who picks up the phone?', with a single answer control (chip grid, text field or drop zone) and a Continue button that Enter also triggers. Steps: source (paste a job description, product URL, CRM note or call transcript), buyer role, industry, objections, difficulty and personality, rep goal, then review. A summary card assembles at the right edge as answers arrive. Review shows editable fields and a generated opening line. 'Skip all to form' stays visible.
screens.key_components: One-question component, source drop zone (PDF, URL, paste), assembling summary card, editable review screen, footer chip 'Generated with gpt-4.1-mini, structured output', Skip all to form.
screens.change_vs_today: New screen. Replaces hand-filling a ten-field scenario form, which survives as the escape hatch.

screens.layout: Single column, max 720px. Persona header: avatar, name, role and a one-line situation. Question card: 'How will you open the call?' with a text box. On submit, a three-line pre-flight note scores the opening against the greeting criterion before the call starts. Below: the six-step talk track as a horizontal stepper, rubric weights as a stacked bar with a legend, and likely objections as chips. Footer: Voice and Text as two large selectable cards with a live mic-level meter, and one primary Start call button.
screens.key_components: Persona header, opening pre-flight check, talk-track stepper, rubric weight bar, objection chips, mic meter, Voice and Text cards, Start call.
screens.change_vs_today: Replaces the precall card with a collapsed talk track and rubric by one ordered briefing and a warm-up question, so no rep enters a call without a plan.

screens.layout: Desktop 12-column dark cockpit with no side nav. Left 7 columns: the caller as a Pulse orb (a ring driven by audio level) with a state label, 'Caller speaking' or 'Your turn', then the last six transcript turns, expandable. Right 5 columns: a coach rail with three modules: live rubric (six bars, Geist Mono scores, delta arrows), talk-track dots for steps 1 to 6, and a cue stack capped at two amber cards with 'Say this' and dismiss. A coral objection bar pins to the top. Bottom bar: push-to-talk or text, timer, mute, hints toggle and End and grade (hold 2s).
screens.key_components: Pulse orb, transcript with turn markers, live rubric meters, talk-track dots, capped cue stack with auto-dismiss, objection alert bar, timer, hold-to-end button.
screens.change_vs_today: Today's live screen is a chat app with no coaching or scoring. Coaching becomes private to the rep (the persona never sees cues) and scores update every turn.

screens.layout: One page with a sticky section nav. (1) Verdict: 72px Geist Mono grade, goal pill and one plain-English takeaway. If the LLM grader fails, a 'Graded by keyword fallback' chip with Re-grade appears. (2) Skill radar: six criteria, this call against the last three. (3) Moment timeline: horizontal track with a score sparkline and tags (Strong, Missed, Objection); clicking a moment opens a drawer with quotes and rubric rationale. (4) Redo this moment: replays the 60 seconds around the weakest turn as a short role play. (5) Full transcript, collapsed by default.
screens.key_components: Grade ring, goal pill, custom SVG radar, moment timeline with sparkline, evidence drawer, Redo this moment, collapsed transcript.
screens.change_vs_today: Replaces one long card scroll with a verdict-first summary, moment-level evidence and a one-click redo.

screens.layout: Top strip: four tiles (sessions, average, best, time practised) with Geist Mono numbers and 30-day sparklines. Main grid: left 8 columns is a line chart of score per criterion over time with six toggleable series (top two on by default); right 4 columns is a skill radar, first call against latest. Middle: a 26-week heat calendar of practice minutes. Bottom: a 'Your next rep' card recommending a library persona aimed at the weakest criterion, and an objection tracker showing the three most-missed objections.
screens.key_components: Stat strip with sparklines, criterion line chart with series toggles, skill radar, heat calendar, next-rep recommendation, objection tracker.
screens.change_vs_today: Replaces four number tiles and a plain list with trend lines, a recommended next persona and objection tracking.

screens.layout: Team selector and date range at the top. Three status tiles (On track, Needs practice, Stalled), each with a count and change against the previous period. Main: rep table with columns for rep, current persona, last call, score trend sparkline, weakest criterion, status and actions. Row click opens a right drawer with the last five debriefs, supervisor notes and an Assign persona picker drawn from the library. Bottom: a review queue of calls flagged by low grader confidence or a manager-marked moment. CSV export in the header.
screens.key_components: Status tiles, rep table with sparklines, assignment drawer, supervisor notes, review queue, CSV export.
screens.change_vs_today: No manager surface exists in the UI today. This adds one on the existing org and supervisor-notes data model.

screens.layout: 390px wide. The caller orb fills the top 30% with name and a 'Your turn' pill. The transcript scrolls in the middle showing the last three turns. One cue card floats above the composer, full width, with a 44px 'Say this' tap target. A coach handle at the bottom edge opens a bottom sheet (shadcn Drawer) holding the live rubric and talk-track dots; swipe up to expand. Composer: a 72px push-to-talk as the primary control, with a text toggle beside it. End and grade is a 1.5-second long-press in the sheet. 16px gutters, no horizontal scroll, safe-area insets respected.
screens.key_components: Orb header, three-turn transcript, floating cue card, coach bottom sheet, 72px push-to-talk, long-press end.
screens.change_vs_today: Today the End button shares the composer row and there is no coaching on mobile. Coaching moves into a sheet and the mic becomes the primary action.

live_coaching_and_scoring: The design assumes a separate coach stream, not the persona (which stays forbidden to coach). The coach reads each finalized turn and emits typed events: cue, objection, talk-track step and rubric delta. At most two cues are on screen, each auto-dismissing after 8s unless pinned. The live rubric uses incremental grading with the same weighted rubric as the debrief, so the number the rep watches matches the debrief. Latency budget: cue within about 2s of turn end; rubric delta within about 3s; the orb reacts instantly from audio level. Live scores are labeled 'live estimate' until the final grade. Text mode stays clean unless coaching is switched on. Honest gap: the repo has no coach stream yet, so this design only meets the bar once that engine exists.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: 15 sales jobs at launch (SDR cold call, SDR inbound, AE discovery, AE demo, SaaS price objection, insurance quote, mortgage pre-approval, real estate buyer, solar consult, home services estimate, auto dealership, medical device rep, B2B procurement, recruiting screen, retail returns, customer success renewal, collections), about 10 personas each, targeting 150+. Each persona is one JSON file in personas/ validated by a zod schema. The library builds from those files, so contributors add personas by pull request. Wizard: seven one-question steps. The GPT call (default gpt-4.1-mini) returns structured output checked against the same schema. The user edits the result, then saves it or exports a PR-ready file. A similarity check warns about near-duplicates.
signature_moments: The answer summary card assembles itself as you answer, so the persona feels built with you rather than filled in.
A cue card whispers 'Ask about unit age first' while the caller is still talking, then dismisses itself.
The debrief opens with one sentence and one grade, and 'Redo this moment' replays the 60 seconds around your weakest turn.
The orb is a Realtime-voice pulse that is labeled with the active voice provider, so users always know which OpenAI model is talking.
openai_fund_angle: Showcase: a Model Lab card in settings and the footer lists each role and its model: caller voice (OpenAI Realtime API or ElevenLabs Agents, switchable), live coach and grader (gpt-4.1-mini default) and the persona wizard (structured outputs). Each role shows a cost-per-call estimate and median latency from the user's own runs. Contributors: 'Good first persona' issues link straight to the wizard export, and every merged persona shows 'by @handle' in the library. A Codex-powered GitHub Action reviews persona pull requests against the schema, which is the PR-review and maintainer automation the Codex for Open Source program funds. Council scores (self-assessed): A 8, B 8, C 7, D 5.2 (only meets the bar once the coach engine exists), E 5.4, F1 SaaS 6, F2 selling to entities 6, F3 not worth building 3 (lower means worth building).

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (about 2 weeks): add Geist, map the new tokens onto existing Tailwind class names through CSS variables, add shadcn Button, Input, Card, Dialog, Sheet and Command; restyle landing and precall in place with the same routes. Phase 2: move built-in scenarios out of localStorage into personas/ JSON files and ship the library and wizard. Phase 3: build the live cockpit and the coach stream. Phase 4: debrief upgrade, progress, then manager view. Each phase keeps routes working, so the change is incremental.

risks: Persona content, not UI, is the bottleneck: 150 personas need sales subject-matter experts to review them.
Live coaching at about 2 to 3 seconds may feel late; cues must read as nudges, not verdicts.
The dense dark cockpit can overwhelm first-time reps, so cue modules should stay hidden until the third call.
Realtime voice cost is the adoption barrier for open-source users without credits; the Model Lab cost estimates must be accurate.
Well-funded competitors (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli) already sell real-call coaching; the differentiator is open, self-hosted and bring-your-own-model.
shadcn copy-in code and Motion add bundle weight; the three.js orb must stay lazy-loaded to keep the landing page fast.
